name: Greyish tan

sections.title: Greyish tan is a soft, warm grey-beige carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Shironezumi, literally "white mouse," and it sits 10.5 units from the plain [[tan]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Shironezumi, written 白鼠, combining *shiro* (white) and *nezumi* (mouse), one of a family of Japanese grey names built on the mouse's coat [1]. No book consulted independently dates the coinage beyond that library gloss, so it is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 68, chroma 12 and hue 58 degrees, in the Oranges family by our classification, read by most eyes as a warm beige rather than a true grey [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[sweet-pea]], [[mushroom]], [[mauve-blush]] and [[light-cinnamon-drab]], at 2.9, 3.3, 3.5 and 3.6 ΔE [1]. A darker, more neutral cousin in the same descriptive family is [[greyish-umber]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 1,260 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 5.3 percent, as photographed, most often as a highlight [2]. The earliest dated match is an Egyptian ostracon fragment dated to roughly 1295 BCE in the archive's year field, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Among Pahari painters specifically, 32 of 118 works carry it, 5.1 times the archive's overall rate[2].
